title: Boss fight: incident night
summary: 02:47, the pager goes off: the web shop is down. A full disk, a config nobody can read, a typo, a CPU hog and a supervisor that gave up. Everything you learned, against the clock (not really, take your time).

nodes.biscotti: the web shop server; read /root/PAGER.txt first

tasks.title: Triage: what filled the disk?
tasks.text: Read the page: `cat /root/PAGER.txt`. Then start where the alarm is loudest. `/srv/shop/data` is 100% full. What is the **name** of the file that filled it?
hints: Mission 16 all over again: `df -h /srv/shop/data`, then `du -sh /srv/shop/data/*` or `ls -lhS /srv/shop/data` (`-S` sorts by size).
A file called `core.<number>` is a **core dump**: a crashed program's memory, written out for debugging. Useful once, enormous always.

tasks.title: Make room
tasks.text: Free space on `/srv/shop/data`: bring it **below 50%**. The order log `orders.log` is the company's income: it stays.

checks.fail_msg: orders.log is gone or empty! Those were real orders. Restart the lab and try again.

hints: Nobody is going to debug that core dump at 3 a.m. (and if they were, you'd move it to a bigger disk, not keep it here).
`rm /srv/shop/data/core.*`. Check with `df -h /srv/shop/data`. If space doesn't come back, remember mission 16: is anything holding it open?

tasks.title: Read the logs, find the next fault
tasks.text: Disk fixed, but the shop is still down. Look at `shopctl status` and the logs in `/var/log/shop/` (`tail` is your friend). The app runs as user **shop** and dies reading its config. Fix the config file's permissions: `shop` must be able to **read** it, nobody else (except root) may read it, and `shop` must not be able to change it.

checks.fail_msg: User shop can modify its own config. Read-only is enough.
Other users can read the config. Give access to shop only.

hints: `tail -n 20 /var/log/shop/shop-api.log`: a Python traceback ends with the actual error, `PermissionError: ... '/etc/shop/shop.conf'`. `ls -l /etc/shop/shop.conf` shows why.
Mission 14's recipe: give the file to the group of the user who needs it, with group read only. `chgrp shop /etc/shop/shop.conf && chmod 640 /etc/shop/shop.conf`.

tasks.title: Spot the typo
tasks.text: There's something wrong **inside** that config file too, and the runbook says what it should be. Fix it. (Running the app by hand shows the error at once: `runuser -u shop -- /srv/shop/bin/shop-api`, then Ctrl+C if it starts.)

checks.fail_msg: The config doesn't say port = {{PORT}} yet.
The edit broke the permissions again (some editors replace the file). shop must be able to read it.

hints: `cat /etc/shop/shop.conf`, and compare it with the port in `/root/PAGER.txt`. Count the zeros.
`sed -i 's/^port = .*/port = {{PORT}}/' /etc/shop/shop.conf`. Then `ls -l` again: the permissions should survive an in-place edit.

tasks.title: Who's eating the CPU?
tasks.text: The pager also said **load average high**. Find what is burning CPU and stop it. (It's not the shop. The shop isn't even running.)

checks.fail_msg: The CPU hog is still running.

hints: `ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -5`, or one snapshot of `top`: `top -b -n 1 | head -15`.
`pkill -f thumbnailer`. Polite TERM is enough this time.

tasks.title: Bring the shop back
tasks.text: Everything is fixed... but the shop still isn't up. Find out why, get it running, and prove it: `curl http://127.0.0.1:{{PORT}}/health` must answer `OK`.

checks.fail_msg: http://127.0.0.1:{{PORT}}/health doesn't answer OK yet. What does shopctl status say?
The shop answers, but not under its supervisor (start it with shopctl, so it gets restarted if it crashes).

hints: `tail /var/log/shop/supervisor.log`: after 5 crashes in a row the supervisor gave up, on purpose, so a broken app doesn't restart forever.
`shopctl restart`, then `shopctl status`, `ss -ltn` and the curl. If it crashes again, the newest lines of `/var/log/shop/shop-api.log` say why.

solution.note: Incident over. Now the part that makes you a boss: write it up. What broke (disk full from a core dump, a config the app couldn't read, a port typo, a runaway job), how you found it, how you fixed it, and what stops it next time: monitoring disk usage before it hits 100%, limiting core dumps (`ulimit -c`), testing config changes, alerting when the supervisor gives up.

steps.cmd: shopctl restart && sleep 3 && shopctl status && curl -s http://127.0.0.1:{{PORT}}/health
